rationale: Registered the successor execution for the open safety direction: the harness adds a case in which the snapshot records a single-voter configuration (the second peer was demoted before the snapshot) while the committed configuration afterwards has two voters again (that peer is promoted after the snapshot), and after the restart it stops the other instance and tries to commit one entry. Construction-time local feedback: with the flag enabled the restarted voter reported latest_config_voters 1 against the 2 in its own log, became Leader without sending a single election request, and completed the commit while the other member was stopped; with the flag disabled it reported the committed two-voter configuration and could neither win leadership nor commit. The harness also restores transport connectivity with still-running peers before the restart, and the earlier cases reproduce their previous outcomes. A revision was declared because the harness, scope, prefix and comparison set changed.

scope.description: Whether a reconstructed configuration smaller than the committed one changes which support counts. Seven in-process cases: the five previously exercised restart shapes (no-snapshot, snapshot-then-RemoveServer, and the within-flag case whose configuration entry stays above the replayed prefix) plus a new shape in which the snapshot records one voter because the second peer was demoted before it and the committed configuration afterwards has two voters because the peer was promoted again after it; that shape runs with RestoreCommittedLogs enabled and disabled. In the new shape, after the bounded leadership wait the other instance is stopped and one entry is committed with a 1000 ms Apply timeout, so the support the completed decision rested on is observable.
assumptions: Real raft instances in one process over the in-memory transport and the in-memory commit-tracking log store from the captured package; the same durable stores are reused across the restart and no membership change is issued after it.
In the new shape the committed configuration has two voters after the promotion while the node's own snapshot metadata still carries the demoted configuration with a single voter.

Every instance of the cluster is stopped before the restart in each case, so after the restart the other member is unavailable in the new shape as well and the surviving instance is the only member of the committed configuration that is running.
The bounded leadership window is 3000 ms (60 x ElectionTimeout = 50 ms) and the commit attempt uses a 1000 ms Apply timeout.
excluded: Disk-backed stores, real networks, crashes during the restart, restarting more than one member, and post-restart membership changes or snapshot installs.

parameters.cases: no_snapshot flag-off/flag-on, config_after_snapshot flag-off/flag-on, config_above_replayed_prefix flag-on, voter_promoted_after_snapshot flag-on/flag-off

experiment.prefix: The single generated test builds each case with MakeClusterCustom(MakeClusterOpts{Peers: 1 or 2, Bootstrap: true, CommitTrackingLogs: true, Conf: inmemConfig with TrailingLogs 10 and RestoreCommittedLogs set per case}); for the new shape it first calls leader.DemoteVoter(non-leader ID), applies 100 commands, takes leader.Snapshot(), then calls leader.AddVoter(non-leader ID, its address) and applies 10 more entries. Before each restart it reads from the surviving instance's own stores the last configuration-carrying log entry (index, decoded server list), the snapshot metadata's ConfigurationIndex and server list, and the commit-tracking store's staged commit index; it stops every instance, rebuilds the survivor's transport on the same address (wrapped in a counter for RequestPreVote/RequestVote and reconnected in both directions to any instance still running) and calls NewRaft over the same stores. It then waits up to 3000 ms for leadership, and in the new shape stops the other instance and calls Apply with a 1000 ms timeout, recording apply_ok, apply_error and apply_ms. Each emitted CA_EVENT line carries scenario and restore_committed_logs as identity plus latest_config_index, latest_config_voters, the server sets, log_config_index, log_config_voters, snapshot_config_index, last_applied, staged_commit_index, the derived config_entry_in_applied_prefix, election_requests, became_leader and the commit outcome.
experiment.responsibility: NewRaft owns the reconstruction of a node's own configuration from its durable stores, and the reconstructed configurations.latest is the only input to the node's own election gating, quorumSize and leader commitment; no component outside Raft is required to repair it.

comparisons.description: New shape with the flag enabled: the reconstructed number of voters is compared with the number of voters in the configuration entry persisted in the node's own log.
Control for the new shape: with the flag disabled the reconstructed voter count matches the committed configuration entry.
New shape with the flag enabled: the instance acquired leadership without sending any election request to another member, while its own log's configuration has two voters.
Control for the new shape: with the flag disabled the instance does seek support from the other member of the committed two-voter configuration.

New shape with the flag enabled: one entry is committed while the other member of the committed configuration is stopped, so the completed decision rested on support that is not a majority of the committed configuration.
Control for the new shape: with the flag disabled the same commit attempt does not complete while the other member is stopped, because the committed configuration requires both voters.
In-run control: the established divergence reproduces in this run (empty configuration against the single-voter entry at log index 1).
In-run control: the established divergence reproduces in this run (the snapshot's two-voter configuration against the single-voter entry at log index 103).

experiment.revision_reason: Adds the voter_promoted_after_snapshot case (demote the non-leader peer, snapshot, promote it again) with a decision-duty step that stops the other instance and commits one entry, restores transport connectivity with still-running peers after the restart, emits election_requests and the commit outcome, and replaces the comparison set with the safety-direction predicates plus two established divergence predicates as in-run controls.
